nodes.title: Order lifecycle keeps validation before creation

intent.outcome: Decide when checkout-v1 may create an order.
intent.value: The authored example has one stable lifecycle rule for success and rejection paths.

decision.decision: Create orders only after cart validation confirms non-empty input and sufficient inventory.
rationale: The valid-cart and invalid-cart examples need one consistent gate.
Rejecting before persistence keeps the tracer bullet small and internally consistent.
consequences: Rejected carts never create partial orders.

intent.outcome: Turn a valid cart into an order.
intent.value: Customers can complete purchases without the example modeling the rest of checkout.

given: a customer has a cart with {n:number} line items
every line item has quantity {q:number} and unit price {price:number}
every cart item is {availability:"in stock"|"out of stock"}
when: the customer submits the cart for order creation
then: an order is created with total {total:number}
the order contains the original cart lines
order creation is rejected because {reason:"empty cart"|"out of stock"}

intent.outcome: Pin the request and response shapes of POST /orders.

openQuestions.question: Does the response carry the inventory-snapshot version the order was validated against?

intent.outcome: Show that a valid cart can become an order.
intent.value: The authored example demonstrates the happy path for create-order.

given: a customer has a cart with {n: 2} line items
every line item has quantity {q: 1} and unit price {price: 50}
when: the customer submits the cart for order creation
then: an order is created with total {total: 100}
the order contains the original cart lines

criteria: The order result contains a stable id.
The returned total matches the authored total — the spec's value, never the test's.

intent.outcome: Define the core terms used by the checkout-v1 order-management slice.
intent.value: Specs, code, and tests use the same vocabulary for carts, orders, and inventory.

terms.cart: A customer-selected set of line items that has not yet become an order.
terms.cartLine: A requested product, quantity, and unit price inside a cart.
terms.inventorySnapshot: The available quantity for each product at validation time.
terms.order: The persisted result of accepting a valid cart.
terms.orderTotal: The sum of all accepted cart line subtotals.
